summary:
M8 (Documents and period close, C4) is built. I didn't run `next build`/`next dev`, and uploads/downloads haven't been tried against the live Supabase project.

1. **Shared panel** — `PeriodClosePanel` (in `src/components/documents/`) is used by both the company portal and the ScaleUp pages.
   - It lists the quarter and half-year closes, newest first. Each is a card that folds away; open closes start expanded.
   - Each card shows:
     - the label, type, date range and status;
     - the months in the period with their status, red when overdue, each linking to the month's update (company side) or review page (ScaleUp side);
     - "x of y months submitted" and what is still needed before confirming;
     - a totals table: revenue, gross profit, gross margin, net profit, net margin, cash at period end, average monthly burn, full-time and part-time headcount.
   - While a close is open, the totals are live from the submitted and approved months, counted from the later of the period start and the reporting start month (or the first submitted month if there is no start month).
   - Once confirmed, it shows the totals stored at confirmation next to any restated figures, the reason, and who confirmed and when.
   - Management accounts and supporting files are listed with name, version, size, uploader and date, plus a Download button.
   - On the company side, ScaleUp staff always appear as "ScaleUp". On the ScaleUp side they appear as "Name (Fund Admin)".
   - There is also an "Other documents" area for files not tied to a close. Exited and written-off companies are read-only, with a banner.
2. **Upload** — the dialog lets you pick or drag a file and choose the document type.
   - The file is checked for type and the 25 MB limit.
   - The server signs an upload to exactly the storage path the database accepts.
   - The browser then uploads straight to Storage with the file type taken from its extension, and the server saves the `documents` row. The database assigns the version.
3. **Confirm** — the dialog shows the calculated totals and lets the owner (or a Fund Admin on their behalf) restate figures to match the management accounts. A reason is required when anything is restated, then it calls `confirm_period_close`.
4. **Download route** — `GET /api/documents/[documentId]/download`:
   - reads the document with the caller's normal database access (not visible → 404) and re-checks access to the company;
   - signs a 60-second link using the caller's own Storage access;
   - writes a "download" entry to the audit log, and refuses the download if that entry can't be written;
   - then redirects to the link.
5. **`/admin/documents`** — the portfolio view has a period selector (Q3 2026, H2 2026, …) and a fund filter, four summary tiles, and a table per company: fund, status (or "Ready to confirm", "Not yet reporting", "No close"), months submitted x of y, management accounts count, restated, confirmed date. `?company=<id>` opens that company's panel. Fund Admins can upload and confirm there on the company's behalf; Super Admins and Fund Admins can reopen a confirmed close with a reason.
6. Both routes have loading skeletons and a friendly error page with "Try again".
deviations: Download audit entity: the brief says log_audit_event("download", "document", …); I used "documents". That is the table name the audit triggers write for uploads, the example in contract §2.4, and what tests/db/audit.test.ts uses, so uploads and downloads of a document group together in the audit log. Summary = the file name as briefed; the extra data holds {file_name, version, doc_type, period_close_id}. It is a one-word change if "document" is preferred.

Storage signing never uses the service-role client. Downloads use the caller's own Storage access, as the brief says (contract §2.8 mentions the service role). Upload links are signed the same way, so Storage checks the upload permission as the uploader when signing. M8 never calls createAdminClient.

HEAD requests to the download route return 405 (Allow: GET). Next.js otherwise answers HEAD by running the GET handler, which would sign a link and write a download audit entry for a download nobody made.

Restatement: people restate amounts and headcounts only. The gross and net margins are recomputed on the server from the restated (or calculated) revenue and profit, and stored only when they change. Figures equal to the calculated ones are dropped, and a reason is required only if something still differs. The database would also accept typed margins; the app never sends them.

Download errors: browsers get a small HTML page with a 'Go back' link; other clients get JSON {error}. Statuses: 401, 403, 404 (not visible or file missing from storage), 500 (audit entry couldn't be written, so no download), 502, 503.

The file name offered on download is cut down to plain letters, digits, spaces, '.', '_' and '-'. The Supabase client encodes the name twice, so other characters would come out garbled. Example: 'Relatório (final).pdf' downloads as 'Relatorio final.pdf'. The stored display name keeps the original.
Uploads to a confirmed close are allowed, as the database allows. The dialog says the file joins the close's history and the confirmed totals don't change.
Extra URL parameters: portal ?close=<closeId> opens that close; admin ?period=Q3-2026, &fund=<code>, and ?company=<id> with optional &period=… or &close=… to open a specific close.
Both pages call open_due_periods() when they load (failures are logged, not fatal), so a close appears as soon as its last month opens. The contract describes this for the tracker and portal pages.
Page props are typed explicitly (params/searchParams as Promises) rather than with the generated PageProps helpers, as the brief instructs.
verification:
- `npx tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors in the whole project at the time of the final run (0 in M8 files).
- `npx eslint src/components/documents src/lib/actions/documents.ts "src/app/portal/[companyId]/documents" src/app/admin/documents src/app/api/documents tests/features/m8`: clean.
- `npx vitest run tests/features/m8`: 6 files, 72 tests, all pass.
  - Pure helpers (document-rules, totals, view-model, action-schemas): file type, size and name rules; storage paths checked against the database's path rule and Storage's key rule; download names; storage error wording; totals and restatement derivation; months counted per close; live totals; document grouping, versions and "latest"; "ScaleUp" labels (B28); close ordering; period keys and selector options; portfolio rows and summary; the Server Action input checks through toActionError.
  - render.test.ts renders the whole PeriodClosePanel and the portfolio table (data loading mocked) for owner, contributor, exited company, fund admin, partner, viewer and super admin. It checks buttons, links, "ScaleUp" labelling, the disabled Confirm button and the read-only state.
  - sql-parity.test.ts runs against the real migrations in the PGlite harness from tests/db (imported, not edited):
    - paths from buildDocumentPath pass the storage upload policy and the documents trigger; versions are assigned;
    - a Fund Admin upload is audited as on behalf, and a partner is refused;
    - the restatement from deriveRestatement is accepted by confirm_period_close;
    - my live totals equal the stored computed totals exactly, including decimals and negative gross profit, a month sent back, a later reporting start and a cleared start month.
- `npx vitest run tests/unit tests/data tests/features/m8`: 19 files, 307 tests, all pass.
- Not run: `next build`, `next typegen` and the dev server (per the rules). The Storage upload/download round trip hasn't been tried against the hosted Supabase project.
openQuestions: Should uploads be blocked once a close is confirmed? They are allowed now (the database allows it) and the confirmed totals don't change; a company that wants the totals revised needs the close reopened.
Audit entity for downloads: "documents" (table name, matches upload audits) or the brief's "document"?
Business sign-off for BRD §13: restated margins follow the restated revenue and profit (derived, not typed in); only figures that differ from the calculated ones count as restated.
Is it acceptable that the downloaded file name drops accents and special characters? This works around the Supabase client encoding the name twice; the display name keeps the original.
Files are uploaded with the file type taken from their extension (a CSV that Windows reports as Excel is uploaded as text/csv), so the bucket's type list always accepts them. OK?
notesForOtherModules:
Routes M8 provides:
- `/portal/[companyId]/documents`, optional `?close=<closeId>` to open a specific close.
- `/admin/documents`, optional `?period=Q3-2026` (default: newest period) and `&fund=<fund code>`.
- `/admin/documents?company=<companyId>`, optional `&period=Q3-2026` or `&close=<closeId>`.
- `GET /api/documents/[documentId]/download`: 302 to a 60-second signed link, audited; HEAD returns 405.

Server Actions in src/lib/actions/documents.ts, each returning ActionResult:
- `prepareDocumentUpload({companyId, periodCloseId|null, docType, fileName, sizeBytes})` → `{bucket, path, token, contentType}`
- `saveDocument({...same, path})` → `{id, version, docType}`
- `confirmPeriodClose({companyId, closeId, restated?: {revenue_total?, gross_profit?, net_profit?, cash_in_bank?, avg_burn_rate?, headcount_ft?, headcount_pt?} | null, reason?})`
- `reopenPeriodClose({companyId, closeId, reason})`

Shared component: `PeriodClosePanel` from `@/components/documents/period-close-panel`. It is an async, server-only component with props `{ company: CompanyRow, mode: 'company' | 'scaleup', ctx: PermissionSubject, focusCloseId?, focusPeriodLabel? }` and works out upload, confirm, reopen and export rights itself. M1 can link its company page to `/admin/documents?company=<id>` or embed the panel.
M7: the home period-close card links to `/portal/${companyId}/documents`. It can add `?close=${close.id}` to open that close.

M9, document pack: each close card shows 'Download all' → `GET /api/exports/documents/<companyId>?closeId=<closeId>` to users allowed by canExport (every ScaleUp role; owners of their own company). Please implement it with exactly that parameter name.

M9, audit viewer: downloads are logged with action 'download', entity 'documents', entity_id = document id, company_id, summary = file name, data {file_name, version, doc_type, period_close_id}. Upload rows come from the audit trigger with entity 'documents' (marked on behalf for Fund Admins).

M9, C4/LP export: `period_closes.restated_totals` may contain derived gp_pct/np_pct. `parsePeriodTotals`, `parseRestatedTotals` and `effectiveTotals` in `@/components/documents/totals` are client-safe and can be reused.

Integrator:
- No nav or proxy change is needed: Documents is already in both sidebars, and the proxy's 401 JSON covers signed-out /api requests.
- Please add the BRD §13 build decisions listed in openQuestions (restated margins are derived; confirmed closes accept new document versions; download audit entity naming).
- tests/features/m8/sql-parity.test.ts imports tests/db/harness.ts, scenario.ts and fixtures.ts (read-only), so a change to those APIs may need a matching update there.
